story:
Enki was the Mesopotamian god of wisdom, crafts, fresh subterranean waters, magic, and incantations, who ruled the Abzû. His wife was Damgalnuna, and their children included Nanshe, Asalluhi, Marduk, and Enbilulu. His attendant deity was Isimud, and his servants included the lahmu, the kulullû, and the Seven Sages.

Enki was credited as the creator of mankind, fashioned from clay. In one myth, Enki devised the plan to create a new being meant to take over the labor of the gods. In another, he worked together with the goddess Belet-ili to create man from clay mixed with divine blood. When the god Enlil later sought to destroy humanity by sending a flood, Enki had sworn an oath not to reveal this plan, so instead he warned his human protégé by speaking to a reed wall, allowing humanity to survive. In a later account, the creation of man was instead described as a joint effort between Enki and his son Marduk.

Enki also acted as a clever problem-solver among the gods. In one story, to calm the heart of the warlike goddess Ishtar, he fashioned a double of her out of clay to serve as her adversary. In another, he outwitted the warrior god Ninurta, who had been plotting against him. In the story of Adapa, Enki gave instructions that allowed Adapa to ingratiate himself with three gods. In the Kumarbi cycle, Enki served as a problem solver and kingmaker among the gods.
